slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop feeling awkward
eating alone in public
(and actually enjoy it)
Pick the right seat. A spot at the bar or a table by the window. Watching the street or the kitchen gives your eyes somewhere to go, and you instantly feel less on display.
Order with confidence. "Just me tonight, thanks." Said with a smile, it sounds relaxed, not lonely. Staff love solo diners who are easy and friendly, and you often get better service.
Remember nobody is thinking about you. The couple next to you is talking about their week. Everyone in a restaurant is far more focused on their own plate than on your table.
Chat with the staff. Ask what they recommend or what's good today. A short friendly exchange with the waiter makes the meal feel social, even when you came alone.
Bring something to feed your mind. I do five minutes of history, art or science while I wait for my food, and it turns a solo meal into the best part of my day.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app while I wait for my food. History, art, science. A solo meal turns into the best part of my day.

slides.texte_overlay: Put the phone down for the meal itself. Taste the food, look around, enjoy the noise of the room. Eating without scrolling is how a lonely moment becomes a calm one.
Start small, then go bigger. Coffee alone first, then lunch, then a proper dinner. Each step feels easier, and soon going out alone feels like a treat instead of a test.
